title: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ via $^{139}$La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the $Am2m$ Structure
authors: Mitsuharu Yashima, Hongnam Lee, Takumi Ino, Nina Seto, Masataka Kakoi, Hiroya Sakurai, Yoshihiko Takano, Hidekazu Mukuda
abstract: The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via $^{139}$La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the $Am2m$ structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the $Amam$ framework. Within the $Am2m$ framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-$T_c$ superconductivity under high pressure.
summary: This paper re-evaluates the structure and magnetic ordering of La3Ni2O7 using advanced 139La NQR spectroscopy. By adopting the lower-symmetry Am2m structure, the authors successfully explain the observation of two distinct La(2) sites. They conclude that the material exhibits a large-tiny spin-stripe SDW order, suggesting an itinerant magnetic mechanism crucial for understanding high-temperature superconductivity.
main_problem: The study reconsiders the intrinsic ambient-pressure structure and the spin-density-wave (SDW) order in La3Ni2O7, resolving inconsistencies from previous structural assumptions.
main_result: The system adopts the lower-symmetry Am2m structure, leading to a large-tiny spin-stripe SDW order that is itinerant in nature.
method: The research combines experimental measurements using 139La Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance (NQR) spectroscopy with theoretical calculations using DFT+U.
model_or_system: The physical system is La3Ni2O7, which is studied in its ambient-pressure state. The analysis compares the results obtained assuming the Amam structure versus the proposed Am2m structure.
key_observables: NQR frequency (νQ), asymmetry parameter (η), observation of two distinct La(2) sites (La(2)a and La(2)b), and the temperature dependence of the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate (1/T1).
important_parameters: SDW transition temperature (T_SDW = 150 K), magnetic moments (M_bNi vs M_aNi), and the ratio of integrated intensities between the two La(2) sites (observed to be ~1:1).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase is the Am2m structure, which is supported by the NQR data.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the analysis relies on comparing calculated NQR parameters (Table I) with experimental spectra.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the structural discrepancy by showing that the Am2m structure naturally accounts for the two observed La(2) sites via NQR. It then uses this framework to reanalyze the SDW spin configuration, identifying the large-tiny spin-stripe order, and finally concludes the itinerant nature of the magnetism.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed spectroscopic probe into the magnetic ordering mechanism in a strongly correlated nickelate, linking structural symmetry changes to the nature of the SDW state, which is relevant to understanding high-Tc superconductivity.

The inset shows the distri- butions of Hint used for the simulations at T = 120 K, indicating their peak positions Hpeak int and full widths at one-ﬁfth maximum for La(2)a (red) and La(2)b (blue). The experimental spectra are rea- sonably reproduced by the simulations, assuming Hpeak int ≈0.13 T for La(2)a (red curve) and Hpeak int ≈0.42 T for La(2)b (blue curve).

FIG. 3. (Color online) Schematic spin conﬁguration in the NiO2 plane, showing the large-tiny spin-stripe SDW order. The Ni spins (represented by arrows) are oriented approximately along the a axis and form an alternating stripe pattern with QSDW = (0, 1/2) in the orthorhombic basis. The La(2)a and La(2)b sites are projected onto this plane and aligned above the Nia and Nib channels that carry tiny and large MNi, respectively. The gray shading represents the NiO6 octahedra.
